title: Elastic: SANSAR Linux cryptominer fakes GPU readings to hide mining
actor: REF3364 (Elastic's tracking name; financially motivated, unattributed)
summary: Elastic Security Labs describes REF3364, a Linux cryptomining operation seen in late October 2026. Access came through an exposed Ray job agent. The toolkit, SANSAR, adds a kernel rootkit, a modified NVIDIA NVML wrapper that reports 0% GPU use and random temperatures, and an Ethereum-assisted backdoor. Elastic does not know who is behind it and found Turkish comments in the code.
plain: Attackers are secretly mining cryptocurrency on Linux servers with powerful graphics cards, and they fake the card's readings so the load looks normal.
exec: Hijacked AI compute raises costs and takes capacity from real workloads, and fake monitoring readings hide it.
action: Do not expose Ray job APIs to the internet, restrict who can submit jobs, and check hosts for a modified NVML library, unknown DKMS modules such as acpi_thermal_mgr and initramfs changes.

key_findings: Initial access was through an exposed Ray job agent, then a reverse shell and an added SSH key.
A modified NVML wrapper reports GPU utilisation as 0% and substitutes random temperature (36 to 46 C) and power (100 to 200 W) readings.
A kernel rootkit, acpi_thermal_mgr.ko, hides processes, files and sockets and reloads through an initramfs loader.
The netns backdoor fetches its controller address from an Ethereum smart contract.
Turkish-language comments were found in the rootkit source; the operator is unidentified.
recommendations: Check who can submit jobs to GPU clusters and whether GPU monitoring libraries have been modified.

validation.note: Elastic's original (Nov 12) read: REF3364, activity Oct 22-25 2026, exposed Ray job agent, NVML wrapper, Turkish comments match; The Hacker News write-up matches.

review.note: Facts match Elastic original and THN; added Elastic Security Labs (Nov 12) as first primary source, tier primary, validation corroborated
